program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s target binding and behind relation are clear, and the traces consistently support “absent”: the edited image shows the book and flowers separated, with no visible movement toward the requested ordering. Keep the complete/partial/absent distinction tied to progress toward that relation, not merely any repositioning or object change; the trace noting the book was repositioned correctly still finds no relevant progress. One robustness issue is that the edited image contains two flowers while the binding says “the flower”: make the reference selection explicit from the source (the original rose) and compare that same object across images, rather than treating newly appearing flowers as the reference. Preserve an unknown outcome if identity or depth ordering cannot be judged. There are no transport, schema, or dependency failures here; repeated high-confidence traces are consistent evidence, not a reason to alter the criterion.
